rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer: Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the Apollo 11 landing [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The investigating board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The board's report also called the switch failure a serious oversight that all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The notes don't state the board's exact wording on the cause beyond these lines.

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was Oxygen tank No. 2. Its explosion is recorded as "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[oxygen-tank-2]]. The notes link it to the spacecraft that carried it, the command and service module, through a relationship link rather than a fact line [[oxygen-tank-2]]. The command-service-module note says "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" [[command-service-module]].

The Apollo 11 crew member who piloted that spacecraft was Michael Collins. His note says "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[michael-collins]]. The command-service-module note links to him as its pilot [[command-service-module]].

During the landing, he stayed in lunar orbit. His note says "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[michael-collins]].

The notes do not say anything more about what he did during the landing.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The "mailbox" was an improvised CO2 scrubber adapter. Engineers devised it from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape, because the command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"; [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The crew built it from radioed instructions [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The engineers who devised it were at Mission Control in Houston [[mission-control-houston]] "[stated] Engineers there devised the Apollo 13 carbon dioxide scrubber adapter (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The brain does not give the step-by-step build process or the exact sequence of the radioed instructions.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Here are the 1970 dates the brain records for Apollo 13, in order. The citations now copy each fact line exactly, including its `[stated]` tag.

1. **1970-04-06: Blood tests.** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10: Crew swap.** The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference, replacing Mattingly with Jack Swigert as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11: Launch.** [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13: Oxygen tank explosion.** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded about 56 hours into the flight. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" The mission goal also changed from a Fra Mauro landing to a safe return that day. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17: Splashdown.** The crew had used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down that day. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970: Review board report.** The Cortright board's report on the explosion was published. It called the switch failure a serious oversight that all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The brain gives only the month for the June report, so its place in the order is approximate.

citations.quote: [stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)
[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)
